title: Page Refresh Brief
summary: Diagnose whether one page should be refreshed, consolidated, preserved, or routed to another intervention, then prepare a verification-ready brief.

required_inputs.description: The canonical or intended URL of the page to diagnose.

scope.guidance: After the blocking target-page precheck passes, inspect no more than three representative queries needed to distinguish intent and page role.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot support a search-intent or result-pattern diagnosis without current result evidence.

evidence_plan.fallback: If execution passed readiness but cannot produce result evidence for the relevant input, return a constrained incomplete diagnostic with the failure class, unresolved question, valid remaining observations, prohibited claims, recovery route, and resume condition; defer disposition and emit no implementation handoff.

scope.guidance: Inspect identification, canonicalization, and observable indexability directives for the one target page during the blocking precheck.

completion_without.limitation: The target page cannot be identified and compared reliably without its current metadata.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete diagnostic with the unresolved target evidence named.

scope.guidance: Inspect observable access, crawl, rendering, redirect, status, and indexability signals for the one target page before result inspection or content comparison.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot rule out an earlier technical blocker before recommending content work.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete diagnostic rather than assuming the page is technically eligible for refresh.

scope.guidance: Only after the blocking target-page precheck passes, read the target and no more than three representative comparison pages. An authorized full-page read or supplied capture can satisfy this stage when its identity, time, completeness and retained material support the actual claim. Record the producer and coverage. A search snippet or partial extract cannot establish full-page coverage.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot diagnose content gaps, preservation needs, or page overlap without full-page evidence.

evidence_plan.fallback: When full-page evidence is required for comparison, request an adequate capture or authorized read and return an incomplete diagnostic for the unresolved comparison.

scope.guidance: Use one authorized search context for the exact target and property, with reporting periods, filters, and observed URL and query scope where material.

evidence_plan.condition: Use adequate supplied or authorized connected first-party search evidence when an observed visibility change or account-level indexing finding can change the page decision.

completion_without.limitation: The brief cannot claim first-party search performance or indexing state.

evidence_plan.fallback: Continue with supported public page and search evidence. Identify the missing search report or URL observation if it is needed for the requested decision.

scope.guidance: Use one authorized analytics context for the exact target, reporting periods, source slice, and decision objective.

evidence_plan.condition: Use adequate supplied or authorized connected analytics evidence when engagement, measured conversions, revenue, or other observed behavior can change the page decision.

completion_without.limitation: The brief cannot claim first-party engagement, conversion, revenue, or other measured behavior.

evidence_plan.fallback: Continue with supported page and search evidence. Identify the missing analytics observation if it is needed for the requested decision.

steps.instruction: Confirm the page objective, site role, target market, known query context, and constraints on changes. When given a performance finding, establish its target, source, reporting periods, evidence references, objective, uncertainty, and proposed next question. Reuse adequate evidence and check whether its dates and scope still support the decision.
Inspect current authorization, availability, and cost for page retrieval, result inspection, comparison, and any necessary additional first-party acquisition.

First inspect observable access, crawl, rendering, redirect, status, canonicalization, and indexability directives or signals for the target. If a blocking signal makes result comparison misleading, stop before inspect-serp and return the supported technical conclusion as a completed bounded diagnostic without claiming first-party index state. Only after the precheck passes may the method acquire the target content and continue comparison.
After the target precheck passes, inspect a bounded current result set for no more than three representative queries to identify observed intent, result types, and viable page patterns.
Compare the target with representative results and relevant site pages without treating competitor phrasing as a drafting template.

Classify supported causes across technical access, site role, intent, planning, content, authority, and operational evidence. Treat every automated content or quality score as an evidence input rather than an editorial verdict: inspect its underlying observations, reconcile material conflicts with independently observed page evidence, and state unresolved discrepancies before reporting a score-derived conclusion. Check whether the current target suits the observed intent before recommending optimization. Evaluate overlapping pages in light of their distinct roles and the evidence of actual competition for the intended destination.

Return the supported disposition, including preservation, refresh, technical repair, consolidation, further investigation, or another justified action. When implementation is justified, link the handoff to the target, objective, decisive observations, uncertainty, implementation boundary, and a practical verification check. Specify applicable preservation, change, removal, addition, proof, linking, and acceptance requirements.

evidence_requirements: The diagnosis records current page evidence and result-page conditions.
Every proposed change or preservation constraint links to an observation or explicit user requirement.
Competing technical, strategic, authority, and operational explanations are considered before prescribing content.
First-party performance claims appear only when supplied or returned by an authorized source.
Automated scores support conclusions only when their underlying observations were inspected and material conflicts were reconciled or recorded as unresolved.
A performance finding can guide the next check. Complete the current technical precheck, page and intent assessment, and required evidence checks before recommending content changes.

Support a current target recommendation with appropriate live page and intent evidence. For creation or consolidation, show distinct unmet intent or harmful competition and the evidence needed for that action.
stop_conditions: Stop before inspect-serp when an observed blocking access, crawl, or indexability signal makes page comparison misleading; sufficient blocker evidence supports a completed bounded technical diagnostic even though comparison did not begin.

Treat unmet authorization, availability, input, parameter, or budget requirements as readiness failures: stop before starting the affected paid or protected evidence step and report the precise prerequisite.

Treat a capability that passed readiness but could not produce required evidence for the relevant input as an execution-time evidence failure: return a constrained incomplete diagnostic with defer disposition and no implementation handoff.
Treat a successfully completed capability with no observations as completed empty evidence rather than as an execution failure.
Return an incomplete diagnostic when the page or required market context cannot be resolved.
completion_criteria: The supported intervention and disposition are explicit.
The diagnostic distinguishes observations, interpretations, competing explanations, and unknowns.

An execution-time required-evidence failure identifies the exact gap and failure class, supported and unknown layers, valid remaining evidence, prohibited conclusions or interventions, recovery route, resume condition, defer disposition, and omitted implementation handoff.
Any implementation handoff is self-contained and contains no finished copy.
Verification criteria protect useful current material and test required changes.

output_contracts.condition: Emit only when the diagnostic is complete, its disposition is proceed or conditional, and the evidence required for the specific intervention supports an implementation-ready action.

bounds.sample_guidance: Inspect only enough representative results and site pages to distinguish intent, page role, and material gaps.
